reviews.title: PAID AND WAS CANCELLED
reviews.text:
Unfair Trade Practices and Monopolistic Coercion

For years, TalkingParents provided a baseline functional tier that allowed litigants to meet court-mandated communication requirements. You have since unilaterally eliminated free access tiers—forcing essential communication behind mandatory paywalls while providing an identical, un-updated software interface.

 Trapping court-ordered litigants who have already paid via valid app store channels, refusing to sync verifiable transaction records, and forcing them into a state of legal jeopardy unless they capitulate to your billing errors constitutes a clear violation of the Florida Deceptive and Unfair Trade Practices Act (FDUTPA - Fla. Stat. § 501.201 et seq.), breach of contract, and bad-faith business practices.

The most annoying part is that every time a call is incomplete because of the faulty app. Meaning that the app crashes it deducts time from you.

reviews.title: Company is dishonest and disingenuous. Intentionally puts abuse survivors in danger.
reviews.text:
TalkingParents is a court ordered communication system that has created an impossible catch-22 that knowingly puts vulnerable parents and children in danger.

This is long, but please read, especially if you are a financially struggling parent and/or having to deal with a high-conflict, litigious, or abusive coparent. 

My experience with TalkingParents has been profoundly disappointing and frightening, and I believe anyone dealing with a high-conflict co-parent should think very carefully before relying on this company.

TalkingParents is not simply an optional communication app for many of its users. In my case, use of TalkingParents is court-ordered to as a means to help me stay safe due to the co-parent's history of abusiveness. When our parenting plan was entered in 2022, TalkingParents offered a free tier, which are utilized up until recently. In June 2026, the company arbitrarily eliminated that free option, turning what had been a free court-ordered service into an ongoing financial obligation that I cannot afford.

That distinction matters enormously when you are dealing with a high-conflict or personality-disordered co-parent.

When communication is court ordered to occur through a specific platform, losing access isn’t merely inconvenient. A high-conflict co-parent can seize on any perceived technical or procedural violation and attempt to turn it into an allegation of noncompliance or contempt of court. reviews.title: Horrible functionality and UX
reviews.text: I tried this app with my ex as an alternative to Our Family Wizard (as that app had plenty of problems of its own). This was SO much worse. The UX is awful; you can’t save a message that you’re writing (it just disappears), there is no way to file or categorize sent or received messages into groups (so you remember to respond), and my ex also said it kept crashing on him. These are the issues we have noticed after using it for less than 24 hours. I immediately canceled my subscription.

reviews.title: Disappointing Customer Service and Communication
reviews.text:
I reached out to this company before the promotional period ended and expected a timely response. Unfortunately, there was very little urgency in getting back to me, despite my efforts to resolve the issue before the deadline.

What was most disappointing wasn’t the outcome itself, but the lack of communication and customer service throughout the process. When customers proactively reach out for assistance, they should not have to repeatedly follow up or worry about being ignored.

Based on my experience, I chose to take my business elsewhere. I hope the company improves its responsiveness and communication with future customers.

Also, slow response time by customer service meant I got stuck paying the increased price (I was checking that my data would not be deleted before switching), so it doesn’t appear the company appreciates a loyal customer. We will be switching to Our Famjly Wizard- do yourself a favor and just start with that one.

reviews.title: Are you kidding me?
reviews.text:
I am required by court to use this app with my child's father. I've used it for a few years now and pay the premium plan of $27/month (plus tax) to talk to my child via calls or video. It's worked ok. Has a lot of glitches often. (Dropped calls. App doesn't respond. Can't hear the other party via video calls) Now this app is going up to $39 a month!!!!!!  Disgusting. That's $468/year before Apple's added taxes for an app!  This is outrageous. 
**update: developers respond that they've had limited price increases? Yea ok. Well 12$ a month increase at once is excessive. This app does not share with courts in real time nor does anything truly significant. You can save your chats as pdf's and you can video chat. Again, I've been using this app for years ONLY because I'm required not by choice. As many times as I've printed off how my child's father talks to me and show how he controls and limits my communication with our daughter when she's with him, it changes nothing. Just another broken system taking advantage of parents now price gouging them!

reviews.title: Absurd price increases

Most people can’t afford that in this economy, so don’t be surprised when you see people consistently cancelling their plans. You’re going to run your business in the ground by being greedy!

reviews.title: 5 year user/high conflict case
reviews.text:
I give this one star because initially when I got the service, it was horrible…its web biased interface is horrible. You can’t use the app unless you pay for the premium service. Half the time the app would crash or not send messages when you type them. They would just disappear. Couldn’t see archived content also. They finally fixed it after about two years just recently there was a 44.4% increase in the price. It went from $27 a month up to $39 a month. It seems like the company has now started to capitalize on the amount of coparents who can’t get along and can’t communicate normally. In my situation I don’t have a choice as this is court ordered. I choose to pay to hold the other parent accountable. the other parent recently can’t afford it. I think the price increase is crazy considering the users are already incurring the cost of attorney fees and court cost. Not to mention the app does not work as well as it should for the price. Fingers crossed for full custody🤞so I don’t have to keep paying for this trash app and the price.

Willing to bet I get some AI generated reply to my review, it’s probably not even gonna be personable. Who knows🤷‍♂️

reviews.title: Excessive Price Increase
reviews.text:
I have been using this app for years, and it started out as affordable.  The price has been going up though without any real updates to justify that increase at all.  Recently, I got an email saying they are going from $12 to $16 per month.  It’s really just starting to feel like the developers are trying to take advantage of single moms and DV survivors at this point.  Which as any of us in family court system know is an issue throughout the entire system.  I will be looking for alternatives.

*Update: When I spoke to support about the waiver mentioned there wasn’t an actual application.  They requested that I email them a long list of very sensitive financial information that would include my child’s social security number.

The Accountable Calling works when it wants and you my find all your calls gone and no one to help you. The picture function is now also broke where you once could attach photos very easily. Now if sends the same picture over and over even when you know you choose the right picture. The Calendar is useless. Our Family Wizard is much better and you can get customer support. It is very hard to change once you start. Make the right choice the first time with an ESTABLISHED business like Our Family Wizard. To add they also MAKE you sign new policies/rules under duress since you HAVE to sign it to stay in compliance with the court orders to get back into your account. Read them carefully because I would never sign or agree to any of those terms if I didn’t need back into my account to only find all my calls are gone and the new calls not captured. DO NOT USE TALKING PARENT IT IS THE WORST

reviews.title: APP IS GOOD BUT..
reviews.text: I have been using this app since 2022. Now my other coparent Abandoned our child in the middle of a re-opened custody case that they initiated in 2022 forcing me to have to rely on an app that would document everything without the he said, she said. Now I have had to pay for this subscription which you guys increased from 9.99/mnt to over 15.00/ mnt. As a single parent on disability and who’s other coparent just abandoned his child, case and refuses to use the app I’m still forced to pay for this app, but I cannot utilize what I need the most. Unless there is a feature that I don’t know how to use. I NEED the CALENDAR to be able to document things on just my end. So I’m only having to use one calendar for my child’s stuff without the other parent being notified ever time I post something or change something that is not for the other parent. It is for me to remember to do something not the other parent. I was harassed by the other parent in 2022 because I tried setting up child’s diet at my home and how she felt as her stomach bothers her from her autoimmune disease. So why can’t I have a separate calendar that doesn’t post to the other parent? If there isn’t a feature could you consider adding this? Maybe a drop down on the calendar for “PRIVATE” or “SHARED w/ COPARENT” option? Otherwise the app is pointless now that the other parent hasn’t and refuses to use it even though it’s court ordered.. Thank you.
